question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $5$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}2lx & =\frac{6}{5} \\ 5\cdot 2lx & =5\cdot \frac{6}{5} \\ 10lx & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to isolate $x.$ To do this, we divide both sides of the equation by $10l:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10lx & =6 \\ \frac{10lx}{10l} & =\frac{6}{10l} \\ \frac{\cancel{10l}x}{\cancel{10l}} & =\frac{6}{10l} \\ x & =\frac{6}{10l}\end{aligned}
$$

We can further simplify the right-hand side as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2\cdot 3}{2\cdot 5l} \\ x & =\frac{\cancel{2}\cdot 3}{\cancel{2}\cdot 5l} \\ x & =\frac{3}{5l}\end{aligned}
$$
